Irene — quick finance read.

We can approve a dealer-fee concession on a per-deal basis provided we document the net revenue recognition and get legal sign-off. My recommendations:

- Cap dealer fee at 5% of gross ARR for the first 12 months (6% is higher than our standard, but we could approve 6% if OrbisAI signs to a 12-month committed spend of >= $300k ARR).
- Require the private offer to carry the public SKU list price (per Evan's request) but treat the dealer fee as a separate contractual rebate to be recorded as contra-revenue. This keeps marketplace invoicing intact but lets us honor the reseller payment outside the marketplace.
- Include a clawback clause: if committed usage falls below 75% of forecast in the first 90 days, Redwood can reclaim the dealer-fee concession (deduct from future invoices or withhold renewal credits).
- Ops note: need to ensure we do not record the dealer fee as a separate payable that creates a different tax/treaty exposure — Laura, can you confirm operational feasibility?

If Ops confirms, I'll loop Legal to add the clause to the master private-offer SOW. Also attaching a quick margin scenario (margin_scenario.pdf) to show the impact at 5% vs 6% at different volume tiers.

Ben
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

Evan — thanks for the clear ask and the PO. Short version: we can accommodate a dealer-fee concession with conditions.

What Redwood can offer today:
- Approve a one-time dealer fee of up to 6% for OrbisAI on the private offer, conditional on:
  * A 12-month minimum commitment at or above $300k ARR (terms to be in the private-offer SOW).
  * Inclusion of a clawback clause (75% usage threshold in first 90 days).
  * Execution of an addendum with Legal acknowledging the dealer fee will be recorded as a contractual rebate (contra-revenue).

Operational notes: the private offer will display the same public SKU list price in the marketplace UI. The dealer fee will be applied via a signed off-market agreement where Redwood reimburses the reseller per the contractual schedule — so DataScale receives the 6% outside marketplace invoicing. This preserves procurement visibility and reseller economics.

Next steps:
